synopsis: ASIL is ISO 26262’s road-vehicle safety-requirement grading scale, ranging from A (lowest) to D (highest); it does not apply by scope to the heavy off-road collision mitigation system considered here [f12060, f12065]. Its hazard assessment combines severity S0–S3, exposure E0–E4 and controllability C0–C3 to yield ASIL A–D or QM, meaning ordinary quality management with no safety requirement [f12062, f12063]. Chapter 3 and the glossary consistently distinguish ISO 19014’s Machine Performance Level (MPL) scale from ASIL, so the program plan must translate ASIL terminology to MPL rather than adopt ASIL targets or passenger-car braking values and scenarios for a loaded haul truck on gravel [f2356, f12066, f15294, f12044, f12071]. Automotive terminology remains common among suppliers and engineers, while ISO 26262 Parts 2 and 8 and ISO/PAS 8800 are retained only as reference material explicitly marked as on-road evidence [f12070, f12067, f12068, f12069]. The facts establish the scope boundary and translation requirement but provide no specific ASIL-to-MPL mapping [f12060, f2356, f12071].
